voiceover: Wedding guests who haven't replied? Here's the exact text. Copy, Paste, Send. Today's awkward message: the guest who's gone quiet. The invitations are out. Some RSVPs are still missing. Here are three versions of the RSVP reminder, from soft to firm. Send them in order. The third one is the hard one. First, one rule. Silence is not a no. Emily Post, Joy and The Knot agree: follow up. Don't assume. You may have heard that twenty percent of guests decline. That's a rule of thumb. Your caterer needs real answers. Here's the part people skip: one message per person. Never the group chat. Version one. Soft. Send it about a week before the RSVP deadline. Hi! Gentle nudge: we'd love to know if you can come. Replies are due Friday. Short, friendly, with the date: that's Emily Post and Joy. Version two. Clear. Send it about a week after the deadline. Hi! The caterer needs our final numbers by Friday. Can you tell us if you're coming? Joy suggests giving the reason: the vendors' deadline. Follow, and tomorrow I'll show you: Five things to settle before you send a single invitation. Now the hard one. Version three: firm, but kind. A phone call. Just checking you got our invitation. Can you tell me today if you can make it? Hate calling? Family or your wedding party can call for you. So: a week before, a week after, then a call. Chasing is easier when you can see who's still pending. At Wedillybird, that's one list: confirmed, pending, maybe, declined. Full texts are in the pinned comment. Save this for later. I'm Norah, Wedillybird's AI host. And next time a guest goes quiet, you'll already have the exact text.

caption:
Guests not RSVPing wedding
Three copy-and-paste messages for guests who haven't replied, from a soft nudge to a short call, plus the order to send them in.
Hosted by Norah, an AI character created by the Wedillybird team.
pinned_comment:
Copy, paste, send. One message per person, never the group chat.

1) About a week before the RSVP deadline: “Hi [Name]! Gentle nudge: we'd love to know if you can come. Replies are due [date]. [link]”

2) About a week after the deadline: “Hi [Name]! The caterer needs our final numbers by [date]. Can you tell us if you're coming? [link]”

3) Still silent? Call: “Hi [Name], it's [your name]. Just checking you got our invitation. Can you tell me today if you can make it?”

Norah is AI-generated.
comment_bait: Which version would you send first: soft, clear or firm?

sources.fact: Check in as the cut-off approaches, keep the message short and state the deadline; a fiance(e), parents or attendants can make the calls

sources.fact: Venues and caterers typically need final headcounts one to two weeks before the wedding, so replies need to be real answers
